title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 209 (Agent’s duty on termination of agency by principal’s death or insanity)

content.overview: When an agency is terminated by the principal dying or becoming of unsound mind, the agent is bound to take, on behalf of the representatives of his late principal, all reasonable steps for the protection and preservation of the interests entrusted to him.
content.glance: On termination by principal’s death or unsound mind, agent must take reasonable steps to protect and preserve interests for the representatives.
content.study: When an agency is terminated by the principal dying or becoming of unsound mind, the agent is bound to take, on behalf of the representatives of his late principal, all reasonable steps for the protection and preservation of the interests entrusted to him.

sections.heading: Termination by death or unsound mind
sections.body: Agency terminated by principal dying or becoming of unsound mind.

sections.heading: Duty to protect interests
sections.body: Agent must take all reasonable steps on behalf of the representatives to protect and preserve the interests entrusted to him.

provisions.title: Agent’s duty on termination of agency by principal’s death or insanity

examples.title: Application of Section 209
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 209 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 209?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 209. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 209
distinctions.body: Section 209 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 209 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 209 operates only within the elements and consequences stated in its statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 209 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Confirm termination by death or unsound mind; require reasonable protective steps for representatives.

examTips: Protective duty after death/insanity of principal.
